findings.message: The slice `rows[start : start + size + 1]` returns size+1 users per page, so each page overlaps the next by one row and returns more than requested.
findings.suggestion: return [User(r["id"], r["email"], r["name"]) for r in rows[start : start + size]]

findings.message: The query now loads every user into memory to return a single page, which scales with table size instead of page size. The previous LIMIT/OFFSET query avoided this.
When page is 0 or negative, `start` becomes negative. Python slicing then returns rows from the end of the list instead of an empty or error result.
